races.title: State House, District 7
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mark Speed
cands.bio: Franklin County cattle and timber farmer, business owner and longtime mobile DJ from Louisburg. Franklin County commissioner since 2017, appointed then elected in 2020 and re-elected in 2024. Lost a 2022 state Senate race. Won the District 7 state House seat in 2026.

endorsements.text: In his Ballotpedia survey he lists endorsements from the AFL-CIO and Down Home NC (self-reported).
Ballotpedia lists a voter guide recommendation from the "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" Sway voting group.

cands.gaps: We could not find his exact birthplace town or birth date. We found no record of how he voted on county commission measures such as budgets, tax rates or rezonings. We found nothing on his positions on homestead taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. His campaign site says he fought to lower taxes for working families and fund public schools, but gives no specific votes or measures. We found no documented land-development stance beyond data centers; he said only that district road infrastructure is not keeping up with growth.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia calls him a Franklin County native, and his Ballotpedia survey says he is a lifelong Franklin County resident, with a grandfather and father who also served in local and state office there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Franklin County commissioner since 2017 (appointed, then elected in 2020 and re-elected in 2024); cattle and timber farmer, business owner, and about 25 years as a mobile DJ.
qual.why: He has held local elected office for several years and has run businesses, which fits the middle band. He has no prior legislative service or budget or law career on the record.
qual.label: He has held local elected office for several years and has run businesses, which fits the middle band. He has no prior legislative service or budget or law career on the record.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Said in his Ballotpedia survey that he is opposed to data centers and their rapid expansion into communities, citing air, noise and light pollution, lower neighboring property values and higher household energy costs.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said in his Ballotpedia survey that he is a strong advocate for public education. He said that even with school choice vouchers not every family can afford private school, and that private and charter schools can deny enrollment.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia calls him a Franklin County native, and his Ballotpedia survey says he is a lifelong Franklin County resident, with a grandfather and father who also served in local and state office there.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Wrote in his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: "I am opposed to data centers and the rapid expansion into communities bringing very little in terms of permanent jobs but bringing a lot of pollution." He also cited higher household energy costs.

cands.name: Cory Thornton
cands.bio: Republican candidate for NC House District 7 in 2026. Former U.S. Marine, small-business owner (construction, real estate, entertainment, recycling), MBA holder, deacon at Cedar Rock Baptist Church, and trustee of Vance Granville Community College. Has not held legislative office.
cands.gaps: We found no stated position on data centers, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, or abortion. His campaign site mentions family farms facing pressure from outside land acquisition but does not say what he would do about it. We found no record of him holding office, so there are no actions in office to report. His birthplace and the year he came to North Carolina are not stated. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he has lived in District 7 since age six and that his daughters are raising in Franklin County, but his birthplace is not stated.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owner of multiple businesses in construction, real estate, entertainment and recycling; built an apprenticeship partnership program; earned an MBA; served in the U.S. Marine Corps. No legislative or local elected office is documented.
qual.why: Business owner and manager with no documented prior elected or legislative service, which places him in the middle band. Trustee and church deacon roles are not counted.
qual.label: Business owner and manager with no documented prior elected or legislative service, which places him in the middle band. Trustee and church deacon roles are not counted.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says he will push for property tax relief that doesn't punish families for rising home values, and criticizes property taxes that rise automatically with assessments.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he will fight for parental rights, curriculum transparency and real school choice, and for support for teachers who focus on the fundamentals. He gives no teacher pay figure.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he will cut permitting and zoning red tape that slows new home construction in Franklin and Vance counties, and says regulation squeezes out small farms.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign site says he has lived in District 7 since age six and that his daughters are raising in Franklin County, but his birthplace is not stated.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Says permitting and zoning rules slow construction that would ease prices, and pledges to cut red tape that adds months and dollars to every new home built in Franklin and Vance counties.
